top_signal.title: Millionaires say 'you need capital to start', but how do you get that first capital? Looking for advice for a 19-year-old in a low-tech market.
top_signal.summary: Hi everyone,   I'm 19 years old and looking for some real-world advice and guidance.   I’ve had a huge passion for technology since I was 12 and have been working on building my skills ever since. My ultimate goal is to build significant wealth and achieve financial independence.    I’m based in Iraq, where tech adoption is still relatively low compared to other places. I have plenty of project ideas I’d love to launch, but about 90% of them require starting capital—roughly around \$10,000. Whenever I ask wealthy people in my country how they became millionaires, they usually say they started with a sizable amount of money (like \$100,000), but nobody ever explains how they got that initial capital in the first place to expand their business.   Based on your experience, I’d love to get your thoughts on:      How can I bridge the gap between technology and everyday needs to build a solid business?     What are the best strategies to identify real, pressing problems that people are willing to pay for?     Once I have some starting capital, how can I build multiple projects that generate passive income monthly without requiring my constant manual involvement?      Thanks in advance for your help!       submitted by     /u/Horror_Bridge_7312       [link]       [comments]
